knowledge_items.cause: Motor has overheated
knowledge_items.remedy: •  Check the size of the load, the accel/decel times and the cycle times. •  Decrease the load. •  Increase the acceleration and deceleration times (C1-01 through C1-08). •  Adjust the preset V/f pattern (E1-04 through E1-10). knowledge_items.title: Motor is Too Hot
knowledge_items.description: Motor is Too Hot
knowledge_items.cause: The load is too heavy. If the load is too heavy for the motor, the motor will overheat as it exceeds its rated torque value for an extended period of time. Keep in mind that the motor also has a short-term overload rating in addition to the possible solutions provided below: | The air around the motor is too hot. | The motor fan has stopped or is clogged.
knowledge_items.remedy: •  Reduce the load. •  Increase the acceleration and deceleration times. •  Check the values set for the motor protection (L1-01, L1-02) as well as the motor rated current (E2-01). •  Increase motor capacity. | • Check the ambient temperature. •  Cool the area until it is within the specified temperature range. The drive is operating in a vector control mode but Auto-Tuning has not yet been performed. •  Perform Auto-Tuning. •  Calculate the motor value and reset the motor parameters. •  Change the motor control method to V/f Control (A1-02 = “0”). Insufficient voltage insulation between motor phases. When the motor is connected to terminals U/T1, V/T2, and W/T3, voltage surges occur between the motor coils and drive switching. Normally, surges can reach up to three times the drive input power supply voltage (600 V for 200 V class, and 1200 V for 400 V class). •  Use a motor with voltage tolerance higher than the max voltage surge. •  Use a motor designed to work specifically with a drive when using a 400 V class unit. •  Install an AC reactor on the output side of the drive. | Check the motor fan.

knowledge_items.cause: The motor rated current and the motor no-load current settings in the drive are incorrect. The user is trying to set the motor rated current in E2-01 to a value lower than the no-load current set in E2-03.

knowledge_items.title: Poor Speed Control Accuracy Above Base Speed in Open Loop Vector Motor Control Method
knowledge_items.description: Poor Speed Control Accuracy Above Base Speed in Open Loop Vector Motor Control Method
knowledge_items.cause: The maximum output voltage of the drive is determined by its input voltage. Vector control uses voltage to control the currents within the motor. If the vector control voltage reference value exceeds the drive output voltage capability, the speed control accuracy will decrease because the motor currents cannot be properly controlled. Use a motor with a lower rated voltage compared to the input voltage.

knowledge_items.title: Peripheral Devices Affected by Drive Operation
knowledge_items.description: Peripheral Devices Affected by Drive Operation
knowledge_items.cause: Radio frequency interference may be generated by drive output PWM waveform.
knowledge_items.remedy: •  Change the Carrier Frequency Selection (C6-02) to lower the carrier frequency. This will help to reduce the amount of transistor switching noise. •  Install an Input Noise Filter at the input power terminals. •  Install an Output Noise Filter at the motor terminals. •  Use conduit. Metal can shield electrical noise. •  Ground the drive and motor. •  Separate main circuit wiring from control wiring.

knowledge_items.description: Ground Fault Interrupter Activates When Drive is Running
knowledge_items.cause: The output of the drive is a series of high frequency pulses (PWM), so there is a certain amount of leakage current. This may cause the ground fault interrupter to operate and cut off the drive input power. | Note: | 302
knowledge_items.remedy: •  Change to a ground fault interrupter with a higher leakage current detection level (such as, a sensitivity current of 200 mA or greater per Unit, with an operating time of 0.1 s or more), or one that incorporates high-frequency corrective actions. •  Change the Carrier Frequency Selection (C6-02) to lower the carrier frequency. | Leakage current increases in proportion to cable length. | YASKAWA ELECTRIC SIEP C710606 18C YASKAWA AC Drive – V1000 Technical Manual

knowledge_items.title: Braking resistor
knowledge_items.description: Dynamic braking (DB) helps bring the motor to a smooth and rapid stop when working with high inertia loads. A braking resistor prevents these overvoltage faults. NOTICE: Do not allow unqualified personnel to use the product. Failure to comply could result in damage to the drive or braking circuit. knowledge_items.title: Writing multiple registers (function code 10H) example
knowledge_items.description: Writing to Multiple Registers Function code 10h allows the user to write multiple drive MEMOBUS/Modbus registers with one message. This process works similar to reading registers, i.e., the address of the first register that is to be written and the data quantity must be set in the command message. The data to be written must be consecutive so that the register addresses are in order, starting from the specified address in the command message. The data order must be high byte, then lower byte.

notes: Source: the "heavy" file (498 pages, YASKAWA AC Drive - V1000 Technical Manual, SIEP C710606 18C) per coordinator instruction. The "light" file is a different document: V1000 Quick Start Guide, MANUAL NO. TOEP C710606 15C (YASKAWA Europe, 44 pages); it was not used for extraction.
PDF page index equals the printed page number throughout this manual (e.g. PDF page 349 shows "349").
Page 1 (cover) has no text layer; model_evidence uses the page-2 footer.

Evidence quotes were checked by script against the pdf.js text layer of each cited page (whitespace-normalized). Some range/default values that sit in merged table cells (C1-02..C1-04, d1-02, d1-17, E1-04) are not inside the quoted span; they were read from rendered page images and the note on each record says so.

Footnote markers (<1>, <2>, ...) are defined per parameter group and their meaning differs between groups; meanings were taken from the footnote list of the same group (A/b/C/d: e.g. C and d groups <1> = "Parameter can be changed during run"; E group <1> = "Values shown here are for 200 V class drives. Double the value when using a 400 V class drive.").
Voltage values (E1-05, T1-03) are 200 V class values; the manual says to double them for 400 V class drives.
Rated motor voltage, base frequency (motor) and rated speed exist only as Auto-Tuning inputs (T1-03, T1-05, T1-07); E1-06 is the V/f base frequency.

No documented general rule mapping parameter numbers to MEMOBUS/Modbus registers was found in Appendix C. The B.2 Parameter Table has an "Addr. Hex" column per parameter (e.g. b1-01 = 180, H5-01 = 425), but the table does not state in words that this is the MEMOBUS/Modbus register number; no record was created for it.

Not extracted: comm protocol selection (only MEMOBUS/Modbus RTU on the built-in port, p.426: "Protocol MEMOBUS/Modbus (using RTU mode only)", "Max Number of Slaves 31 drives"), H1/H2 option lists (pp. 369-373), L3-05 details.
H5-01 range "0 to 20 H" and default "1F" are hexadecimal as printed.
0002H broadcast frequency reference is printed as "30000/100%" (p.448), while command register 0002H units are "determined by parameter o1-03" (p.439).

v2 full extraction: parameters parsed from B.2 Parameter Table (pp. 349-398) by script from the stored page text and spot-reviewed; fault/alarm/oPE/auto-tune items parsed from section 6 (pp. 263-291) with cause/solution pairs split heuristically (see details.cause_solution_pairs); verify against the manual when exact pairing matters.

Default values that depend on another parameter, drive model or software version are printed as footnote markers in the manual; for those default_value is null and the footnote text is in setting_conditions.
Ranges/defaults printed in merged cells (C1-0x, d1-xx, d3-0x) are null where not inside the record text unless taken from the earlier hand-verified records.
Parameter importance tiers are assigned by function (commissioning/safety = Important, commonly used = Medium, advanced/monitors/option-card/DriveWorksEZ = Optional).
Modbus register addresses for parameters are the hex "Addr. Hex" column of the B.2 table; not listed individually as registers.
